Someone brought up that this could get muddied by people's "now playing" OSC music statuses. 

There's a fantastic suggestion from another canny post that suggests adding the ability to mark these "status" type messages as "low priority" so they can be filtered out. https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/add-option-to-define-low-priority-osc-chatbox-messages

This would work perfectly with my proposed in-world chatbox system.

details:
I think it'd be really cool if worlds could receive chatbox messages so they can be moved/placed/implemented differently depending on the social dynamics for accessibility purposes.

A friend of mine is working on a world that makes it awkward for me, as a mute, to communicate properly. We got to thinking about how cool it would be to be have chatbox messages exposed to Udon to display them differently in otherwise difficult situations.

I'm pretty sure the team has stated previously that they don't want to implement a native global chat log in the UI and accidentally turn the game into a text group chat, so I think giving world creators the freedom to make chatboxes work best for their world is a really good compromise.

There are tons of situations I've encountered as a chatbox user that could really benefit from the ability to do that. You can hear people you're not looking at, but you can't read chat messages you're not looking at, (obviously,) and that sucks! Having the ability to put chat messages somewhere else in the world would be so nice. To shed some light on this, here are some situations that really suck to be in as a chatbox user:

- Game worlds/video players that require everyone to face a single direction/away from eachother.

- Large worlds with radio systems where everyone is actively moving around. (Exploring a large world in a group, driving, flying, swinging, etc.)

- Worlds with shaders/any other mechanics that generally disrupt the ability to read chatbox messages.

I do think it's worth noting that I understand how this could possibly be abused. Giving world creators access to everyone's chat messages isn't something to be implemented lightly. Maybe this could be done in such a way that the world never actually collects the contents of the message? (Meaning, unable to check for certain words inside a message, etc.)

That being said, I still think this would be amazing for accessibility and something along these lines should be explored by the VRChat team. This platform does such an incredible job at allowing for social interactions that are otherwise impossible in real life, so what's one more attempt at blurring the lines? I'd love to let chatbox users feel just as vocal as anyone else.

Thanks for reading :]
title: Expose chatbox messages to Udon for accessibility purposes
